mcat_description.short: Aircraft hangars are large prefabricated steel structures designed to house, protect, and maintain fixed-wing aircraft, helicopters, and UAVs; sold as engineered-to-order building systems with clear-span frames, cladding, and hangar door packages.
mcat_description.long: Aircraft hangars in the Indian B2B market are predominantly pre-engineered steel building (PEB) systems featuring wide clear-span frames that eliminate interior columns, enabling unobstructed aircraft movement and maintenance. They are supplied as complete structural packages — primary and secondary steel framing, roofing and wall cladding (often sandwich panels or profiled sheets), and large-format hangar doors (bottom-rolling, bi-fold, or sliding) — fabricated off-site and erected at the airport or airstrip. Buyers specify the structure by aircraft type, wingspan, tail height, and operational use (storage-only vs. MRO), which drives span width, eave height, door opening dimensions, fire suppression class, and wind/seismic load design. Applications range from general aviation and private aircraft storage to commercial MRO facilities, helicopter bases, defence installations, and flying school infrastructure.

market_context: Aircraft hangars in India are a niche, high-value, project-based segment within the broader pre-engineered building (PEB) market. The dominant commercial form is the PEB clear-span steel hangar, which eliminates interior columns to allow unobstructed aircraft movement — a fundamental requirement confirmed across multiple technical sources. The Indian market is driven by growth in regional aviation infrastructure (UDAN scheme, new greenfield airports), expansion of MRO facilities, defence modernisation, and increasing private/corporate aviation. Key structural types include T-hangars (nested, for small general aviation aircraft), box/community hangars (open clear-span for mid-to-large aircraft), corporate/FBO hangars, MRO hangars, helicopter hangars, and military hangars. Fabric and tensioned-structure hangars (canvas hangars) represent a secondary sub-segment, used for temporary deployments and defence applications. Indian sellers are concentrated in manufacturing hubs including Rohtak, Lucknow, Ghaziabad, and Vadodara. Structural design must comply with IS 800 (steel structures), IS 875 (wind/snow loads), and relevant DGCA airworthiness infrastructure guidelines; fire protection classification follows NFPA 409 or equivalent Indian standards. Door systems — bottom-rolling, bi-fold, sliding, and hydraulic — are a critical buyer decision point driven by aircraft wingspan and operational frequency. The category is sold as an engineered-to-order product; buyers specify aircraft type, span, height, and use case before a structural design is produced.
